newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Persson denies economic policy U-turn. [CORRECTED 22:17 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Persson denies economic policy U-turn. [CORRECTED 22:17 GMT]

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Thursday that new measures to spend more on welfare would not affect the government's economic policy targets.
"Our economic policy is being maintained and is not affected by the new measures we have proposed," Persson told Reuters.
Persson said on Wednesday he planned to spend 10 billion crowns in 1998 on extra spending on health care, the elderly and education.
Persson also announced an environmental programme (corrects by deleting incorrect reference to cost of programme).

"We can manage these extra proposed measures because the budget outcome has been better than expected. We had forecast higher interest rates and a weaker crown. We are in a positive spiral," Persson added.
